notes.text: Hong Kong mortgages are predominantly floating and priced off interbank rates: 70% of new loans approved in June 2026 referenced HIBOR, 1.3% the best lending rate and 25.1% were fixed, with an average contractual life of 321 months. Because most borrowers reprice with HIBOR, money-market moves reach household debt service within weeks; the HIBOR-linked share has nonetheless fallen from 89.5% in January 2026 to 57% in August 2026 as more borrowers chose fixed rates.

notes.text: The HKMA has unwound most countercyclical lending limits: the 200-basis-point mortgage rate stress test was suspended on 28 February 2024, and since 16 October 2024 the maximum loan-to-value ratio is 70% and the debt-servicing ratio limit 50% for all residential properties regardless of value or owner-occupation, levels the HKMA described as a return to pre-2009 settings. The easing followed a 26.6% cumulative fall in official prices from the 2021 peak to August 2024, and widens access to credit for both owner-occupiers and investors (as of October 2024).

notes.text: All demand-side stamp duties on residential property, namely the Special Stamp Duty, Buyer's Stamp Duty and New Residential Stamp Duty, were cancelled with effect from 28 February 2024 under the Stamp Duty (Amendment) Ordinance 2024. Non-permanent residents and existing owners now pay only ad valorem stamp duty at the standard Scale 2 rates, removing the tax penalty on mainland, foreign and investor buyers.

notes.text: As at 30 June 2026 about 96,000 first-hand private units could reach the market over three to four years, including 19,000 unsold units in completed projects, although private starts dropped to 8,800 units in 2025 from 19,900 in 2024 before reaching 9,700 in the first half of 2026, which leaves the supply outlook later in the decade uncertain. Under the Long Term Housing Strategy the government targets 420,000 units for 2026-27 to 2035-36, split 70:30 between public (294,000) and private (126,000) housing, so public delivery carries most of the planned expansion.

notes.text: Population growth now depends entirely on migration: the provisional mid-2026 population was 7,518,300, up 0.3% year on year, as a net inflow of 39,800 residents offset a natural decrease of 20,400 with births of only 29,700. The government attributes the inflow to talent admission and labour import schemes, making housing demand more sensitive to immigration policy than to natural household formation.

notes.text: The Rating and Valuation Department's territory-wide private domestic price index is published monthly from transactions scrutinised for stamp duty, excluding primary sales and public or subsidised housing schemes, and measures price relative to each unit's rateable value to hold quality constant. Weights reflect transactions in the current and previous 11 months, and the latest months are provisional, so the index lags developer pricing in the new-home market.
